name: Liquidity preference

subjectOf.text: On bankruptcy or termination of the platform, token holders typically have no liquidity preference and no recourse at all once debt holders and outside creditors are satisfied, so unlike a venture capital seed investor with at least a simple liquidity preference, they typically lose everything they invested.
subjectOf.abstract: Again, by contrast, token holders typically lose everything they invested as they have no liquidity preference at all.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: bankruptcy or termination of the promoter's business or platform

subjectOf.text: Token holders typically receive no liquidity preference protecting them if the platform they invested in goes bankrupt or terminates.
subjectOf.abstract: Token holders typically do not receive a liquidity preference that would protect them in the case of bankruptcy or termination of the platform they invested in.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
